notes.topic: New escaping test correctly pins the XSS-escape contract
notes.detail: previewSetKeyboardEscapesTextPerParseMode (FunnelControllerIT.java:32-60 of diff) is a faithful mirror of the proven message-branch previewEscapesHostilePayload (FunnelControllerIT.java:756). It seeds firstName='', sends keyboardText='{user.first_name}' with keyboardParseMode=HTML, and asserts (1) the rendered text is '<script>alert(1)</script>' (positive escape assertion identical to the message branch) and (2) the raw response body doesNotContain('

Round 1 raised 2 minor, non-exploitable notes. Note A (keyboard-branch XSS escaping relied on the shared renderer but had no dedicated test pinning it) is now RESOLVED by previewSetKeyboardEscapesTextPerParseMode. The complementary new cases reinforce the security posture: previewSetKeyboardUnlinkedBotUsesStubSubscriber confirms the stub fallback (no NPE/500 on unlinked bot — the same predictable-state hardening as the message branch), and previewSetKeyboardLabelAtCapNotTruncated pins the clamp boundary (label of exactly MAX_KEYBOARD_BUTTON_TEXT=64 is not truncated; truncation is strictly >, line 491). The clamp itself remains the unbounded-payload defense and is unchanged from round 1.

The only production-code file in the diff (FunnelService.java) changes the clampKeyboardLabels Javadoc (lines 458-469) — expanding the null-vs-empty rationale. Verified against the current file: clampKeyboardLabels body (lines 470-498), renderTextBlock (451-455), the keyboard branch in previewStep (428-441), and the anti-IDOR ordering (requireFunnel first, line 408) are byte-for-byte unchanged. No behavior change, therefore no new attack surface.

notes.topic: OWASP / secrets sweep on the changes
notes.detail: Reviewed all mandatory categories against the diff: no hardcoded secrets (test fixtures use synthetic firstName payloads, no credentials); A01 access control / anti-IDOR ordering unchanged; A03 injection/XSS hardened (above); no SSRF (keyboard branch dereferences no URLs — labels and text are rendered/echoed, never fetched); no insecure deserialization introduced; @JsonIgnoreProperties mass-assignment defense on PreviewStepRequest untouched; no identity fields added to the response (keyboardRows carries verbatim labels only — clampKeyboardLabels strips nothing but length).
